sources.summary: AI-authored hypothetical instructional baseline. No customer discovery, pricing approval or test execution has occurred.

situation.text: The fictional operations team experiences delayed and duplicated service updates across scheduling and downstream dispatch. No actual customer baseline has been measured.

objectives.text: Propose a controlled service integration with explicit reconciliation ownership, measurable duplicate handling and documented recovery acceptance.

value_hypothesis.text: Reduced manual reconciliation may improve service reliability; measure current effort during discovery before claiming any financial benefit or ROI.

technical_approach.text: Use a versioned event contract, idempotency keys, durable retry queue and reconciliation dashboard; retain SSO and a separately reviewed trust boundary.

security_constraints.text: Minimize personal data, restrict production access and retain audit events. Legal basis, hosting location and any certification remain unverified and require competent review.

delivery_approach.text: Discover and baseline first; deliver controlled integration increments; rehearse failure and recovery; transfer only after receiving-owner acceptance.

decision_request.text: Authorize a bounded discovery and confirm accountable scope, technical, commercial and receiving-service owners. No contract or production release is authorized by this proposal.

risks.text: Incomplete source data, unavailable client decisions and integration permissions may delay delivery. Hold the affected milestone for impact review rather than imply unconditional completion.

alternatives.text: Compare retaining the current workflow, a bounded integration pilot and a full replacement. Select only after validated baseline, dependency and total-cost review.

contract_terms.text: Commercial and legal terms remain a negotiation draft: no signed instrument, binding service guarantee or agreed liability allocation exists.
